page: Amazon Web Services i3.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for high I/O throughput and dense local storage. Operating on the Xen hypervisor, it is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processors featuring the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The processor architecture includes 45 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2 instructions, though it lacks newer AVX-512 extensions.

The hardware configuration pairs 488 GB of system memory—equating to 7.62 GB per core—with an integrated local storage array totaling 15,200 GB of NVMe SSDs. It features a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles reflect the instance's legacy CPU design, exhibiting bottom-decile single-core metrics in Geekbench (885.0) and single-threaded stress-ng tests. However, the high core count scales to middle-tier aggregate capacity, delivering a PassMark CPU score of 45,074.88 and 29,386.99 in multi-core stress-ng workloads.

Storage and memory subsystem evaluations show solid middle-tier throughput, sustaining uncached large-block read speeds of 105.96 GB/sec and handling 37.43 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance achieves a PassMark database score of 21,211.88 and static web serving throughput of 25.25 GB/sec. LLM inference performance remains weak for larger models due to legacy instruction set constraints.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the i3.16xlarge prioritizes dense, low-latency NVMe capacity and memory footprint over per-thread compute speed. It presents a viable hardware profile for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, in-memory caches, and high-capacity search indices that require extensive local disk and RAM rather than modern compute-intensive processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.16xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance equipped with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 cores clocked at 2.3 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Hypervisor-managed under Xen, it integrates 488 GB of RAM and 15,200 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, supported by a 25 Gbps network interface and zero GPUs. While single-thread benchmarks place in the bottom decile due to older CPU architecture, multi-threaded metrics remain within average ranges, illustrated by a PassMark CPU score of 45,074.88 and 37.43 million Redis operations per second. With 7.62 GB of memory per core and extensive NVMe capacity, the instance delivers substantial I/O density. It is specifically structured for large-scale transactional databases, data warehousing, distributed NoSQL stores, and log analytics engines requiring massive local high-speed storage.
